assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade theory changed how trade is modelled and measured. It explains exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and new channels for gains from trade, and it underpins a large empirical and policy literature. The contribution is foundational and general.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core model. Helpman, with Krugman, set up the monopolistic-competition trade framework and extended it to firm-level heterogeneity, including the proximity-concentration and offshoring work with Antràs and Yeaple. Redding is a major contributor on quantitative spatial and trade models, but his work is later and more of an extension. Krugman (2008) and Antràs, Yeaple and others are not credited here, which leaves some attribution ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across many datasets and countries. It is now standard graduate teaching and a basis for quantitative trade policy analysis. The timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to pair Melitz with Helpman or with other firm-trade pioneers such as Bernard and Eaton–Kortum.
Helpman's separate protection-for-sale work (B020) overlaps with his credit here.
The Krugman 2008 prize partly covers the monopolistic-competition framework this work builds on.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of differentiated-product demand with endogenous prices (BLP) and dynamic industry models (Ericson–Pakes) is the core empirical toolkit of modern IO. It is also used in antitrust, merger review, trade and health economics. The impact on both research practice and policy is large.
assessment.attribution: The BLP contribution is clearly Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Bresnahan and Reiss (new empirical IO) and Benkard and Levin (dynamic estimation) are also strong contributors, but the three-name limit forces exclusions. The Ericson–Pakes framework is credited mainly to Pakes.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates from 1995 and has been confirmed and extended for three decades. It is very mature and widely adopted in practice.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to include Bresnahan, whose contributions are conceptually distinct.
Criticism of the identification and sensitivity of structural IO estimates.
The field's lower visibility outside specialists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: They showed with granular data that household leverage and credit supply expansions drive booms, busts and deep recessions. This changed macro-finance and informed the post-2008 policy debate. The empirical identification is strong and the conceptual shift is large.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators (House of Debt; Mian–Sufi QJE and Econometrica work). Campbell is eminent for asset pricing and household finance but is a weaker fit for this particular discovery.
assessment.maturity: Their key work dates from 2009–2018 and has been replicated across countries. It is well past the first assessment, though less aged than other candidates.
uncertainties: The Bernanke–Diamond–Dybvig prize (2022) covered adjacent financial-crisis territory.
Debate over the causal weight of credit supply versus demand in some of their papers.
Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from earlier macro-finance prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers think about labour demand, wage inequality and the local costs of trade. It has high policy relevance and links trade and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both strands: the ALM task approach and the China shock. Hanson and Dorn share the trade-shock work. Katz contributed through the skill-biased technical change and race-between-education-and-technology work with Goldin and Autor. The three-name cap excludes Dorn. The task-based framework also draws on Acemoglu and Restrepo, who are not credited here, and Goldin's 2023 prize touches adjacent areas.
assessment.maturity: The ALM paper is from 2003 and the China shock work from 2013. Both have been tested extensively, though the China shock results are still being debated and refined.
uncertainties: Debate over the persistence and interpretation of the China shock and over measurement in the task approach.
Overlap with Acemoglu's 2024 prize and Goldin's 2023 prize.
Difficulty choosing three of four credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave open-economy macroeconomics its modern intertemporal foundations (Foundations of International Macroeconomics, the Redux model). It also framed the exchange-rate disconnect and PPP puzzles. These contributions are conceptually important and directly relevant to exchange-rate pass-through, pricing-to-market and the currency of invoicing.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the unambiguous pair for the Redux framework and the 'six major puzzles' formulation. Others, notably Svensson and Razin, Betts and Devereux, and Gopinath, built important parts of this literature.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the mid-1990s and has been highly influential for three decades. It is very mature.
uncertainties: Attribution of the broader New Open Economy Macroeconomics literature.
Whether the puzzles are seen as resolved discoveries or as open questions.
Overlap with B043 (Reinhart–Rogoff), which also names Rogoff.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian synthesis (nominal rigidities, microfounded Phillips curve, interest-rate rules, welfare-based policy analysis) is the workhorse of monetary policy analysis in central banks. The impact on practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: This is a collective achievement with many contributors, including Calvo, Rotemberg, Taylor, Clarida–Galí–Gertler, Woodford, and Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans, as well as Smets and Wouters. A three-name selection necessarily leaves out important contributors. I favour Woodford (Interest and Prices, optimal policy), Galí (the NK Phillips curve and policy framework) and Taylor (the Taylor rule and staggered contracts).
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of use. Mature and widely confirmed, although the framework was challenged after 2008 and during the 2021–22 inflation.
uncertainties: Severe attribution difficulty with eight listed names and a three-laureate cap.
Calvo's and Rotemberg's roles versus later developments.
Debate on the empirical performance of the framework in recent inflation episodes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression allows analysis of effects across the whole conditional distribution rather than just the mean. It is used throughout labour, development and finance research, and in inequality measurement. It is a major methodological contribution with broad empirical uptake.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (Econometrica 1978) introduced regression quantiles. Koenker's later work developed the theory, computation and applications. Chernozhukov's contributions (inference, instrumental-variable quantile regression) are valuable but are also credited under B029.
assessment.maturity: Developed over more than four decades, with very wide adoption. Mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards a statistical tool as lower priority than conceptual discoveries.
Statisticians' priority claims and the roles of Chernozhukov and others.
Smaller direct policy or conceptual impact compared with the substantive-economics candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A systematic theoretical and empirical study of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It founded modern political economics as a field, with extensive empirical testing, and has had a significant influence on policy discussions.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini (Political Economics, constitutional-rules work) are the clear core. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and development is closely related and often joint with Persson. The three together are a coherent set.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years and well confirmed. Mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity, which may reduce the near-term appetite for the area.
Dispersion of the field across many contributors, such as Alesina, Acemoglu and Dixit.
Causal identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons.
